outlier

OWT-ly-er -- three syllables, stress on the first syllable, OWT. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Outlier is a thing that differs from the rest of a group.

With a week of eighty-degree days, that January was a statistical outlier in the town's weather records.

Example

The class charts everyone's height for a math project. Most bars cluster between five and six feet -- and then there is the outlier: Deshawn, the seven-foot center of the basketball team, whose single bar towers so far above the rest that it drags the class average up by two inches.

An outlier is a data point (or a person, or a thing) that sits far apart from the rest of its group. Outliers matter because they break patterns -- scientists check them for errors, and averages can be badly distorted by a single one.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

exception: An exception is the case a rule does not cover -- everyone came except Lena. It lives in the world of rules and permissions. An outlier lives in the world of measurements: it follows every rule yet sits far from the rest of its group. Break a rule and you are an exception; break a pattern, an outlier.

oddity: An oddity is any unusual, out-of-place thing -- a purple mailbox, a snowstorm in May -- judged on strangeness alone. An outlier is judged on distance: it still belongs to its group but sits measurably far from the rest. Call something an oddity for strangeness, an outlier for distance from the pattern.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

norm: what is typical or standard

average: the ordinary middle of the group

Where it sits · how far from normal it strays — blip → outlier → anomaly

blip vs. outlier: A blip is far milder than an outlier: one strange reading that barely strays and vanishes by the next measurement, while an outlier sits far enough from the group to drag its average and demand a second look.

anomaly vs. outlier: Anomaly is the strongest and strangest: an outlier still belongs to the group it strays from, but an anomaly may defy explanation entirely -- a reading so odd the scientists suspect the instrument is broken.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — out-

prefix — out-: outside, beyond (Old English ut)

root — lie

root — lie: to be situated, to rest (Old English licgan)

suffix — -er

suffix — -er: one that does or is (Old English -ere)

Put it together

Put it together: Outlier is built exactly as it sounds: 'one that lies outside.' It first named rock formations sitting apart from their parent bed and workers living far from their workplace; statistics borrowed it for the data point lying outside the cluster, and everyday English now uses it for any member that sits apart from its group.

Use the root in a new word: underlie

Use the root in a new word: underlie: Geologists spent the field trip mapping the granite that underlies the county.

Root Check

Word Choice

Outlier lives in two registers that share one meaning. In statistics, it is the data point far from the cluster -- always check whether an outlier is an error or a discovery. In general use, it is any person or thing that departs from its group's pattern: an outlier among the season's films, the outlier in a family of athletes. It describes difference from the group, not exile from it.
